meta_description: Sylvia and the Seward Park fir in Seattle, the Kalaloch Redcedar on the Olympic coast and Spokane's heritage trees. {trees} trees across {places} places.
intro: Washington's oldest trees are the Douglas firs and cedars the saws never reached. In Seattle's Seward Park stands a fir that carries the scars of fires from 1508 and 1701, and elsewhere in the city stands Sylvia, a fir that lost her top to the inauguration-day storm of 1993 and is still growing. On the Olympic coast the Kalaloch Redcedar is roughly a thousand years old and half of it lies on the ground beside the half still standing. East of the mountains the country changes and so do the trees: Spokane keeps a Heritage Tree Register of park and street trees, from ancient firs in Indian Canyon that were not worth cutting to an apricot that started in somebody's kitchen garden.
